subject: GRC Connector Decision: SFTP vs API for SOC2 Artifacts
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Schultz <matthew.schultz@clearpathgrc.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: GRC Connector Decision: SFTP vs API for SOC2 Artifacts

Hi Matthew —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're pulling together the delivery pattern for SOC2 artifact handoffs to ClearPath and need to pick a connector approach that meets our security controls while being operationally simple for customers. Two candidate patterns came up:

- Push via SFTP (partner-hosted drop / ClearPath pulls)
- Pull via API (ClearPath calls our API / uses OAuth client)

Key constraints from our side: artifacts may include logs and compressed evidence bundles up to ~250MB, all transfers must be logged for audit/retention, and we need an easy path for customers on dedicated/datasensitive deployments (VPC/private).

Can you confirm which of the above patterns ClearPath supports today, whether you offer signed S3 bucket ingestion (S3 consumer) in place of classic SFTP, and any operational caveats (rotation of credentials, IP allowlists, retention behavior)?

If you have a short comparison doc we can share with our security/legal teams that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to sync live if easier.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
(Attachment: sftp-credentials-template.csv (CSV) )

From: Matthew Schultz <matthew.schultz@clearpathgrc.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearPath GRC Support <support@clearpathgrc.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GRC Connector Decision: SFTP vs API for SOC2 Artifacts

Hi Olga —

Appreciate the note. Short answers up front: we support all three patterns you mentioned, with tradeoffs. I've attached a short matrix. (Attachment: clearpath-connector-options.pdf (PDF))

Summary:
- SFTP drop (partner pulls): simplest to stand up for many customers. We can run an SFTP gateway that pulls from a customer-hosted endpoint, or we can accept pushes to an S3 bucket you provide (we can pull from S3). Pros: simple for large files, easy to batch. Cons: harder to track per-file metadata unless you include a manifest; credential rotation/allowlist management is manual unless you use ephemeral tokens.

- S3 presigned URL (push to S3): we prefer customers push into an S3 bucket and give us read access via cross-account role or presigned URLs for one-off objects. Pros: leverages cloud-native logging (S3 access logs, CloudTrail), easier for VPC/private setups if you use VPC endpoints. Cons: requires customers to manage a bucket or grant cross-account role.

- API pull (OAuth2 + paginated list endpoints): good for small artifacts and real-time items (e.g., config snapshots, short logs). Pros: fine-grained metadata, easier for incremental syncs, better audit trails inside ClearPath. Cons: not ideal for very large files unless you add a two-step upload/presign flow.

Operational notes: we support token rotation and can accept short-lived tokens. For SFTP we recommend using SSH keys per-tenant and rotating quarterly. For S3 ingestion we can consume from an inbound S3 bucket with an agreed lifecycle policy. Retention on our side follows your contract; by default we keep evidence for 90 days unless otherwise requested.

If you'd like, we can run a pilot: inbound S3 bucket + API for high-priority artifacts. Pilot checklist attached.

—Matthew
Matthew Schultz
Partner Integrations Lead — ClearPath GRC
matthew.schultz@clearpathgrc.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GRC Connector Decision: SFTP vs API for SOC2 Artifacts

Olga —

Thanks. I read Matthew's matrix. A few immediate notes from SecOps/Platform:

- We prefer pull patterns where ClearPath authenticates to a scoped API role (least-privilege). That simplifies logging and avoids us having to bless incoming connections.

- For large bundles (>100MB) an S3 presigned upload staged into a dedicated inbound bucket looks most practical. Important: we need server-side encryption using our KMS key and ACLs that prevent public access.

- Audit requirements: every transfer must emit an event to our internal audit stream (Kafka) with artifact metadata (object key, checksum, uploader). If ClearPath pulls, we need them to include the request-id header in callbacks so we can stitch logs across systems.

- Data residency: for customers in EU we need uploads to remain in eu-west-1. Please confirm whether ClearPath can configure region-specific ingestion.

If ClearPath can do S3 inbound + API for small/real-time artifacts and support region-specific buckets, I'm leaning toward that as the default. SFTP could be an escape hatch for on-prem customers but we'd prefer not building SFTP farms.

—Rishi
Staff Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GRC Connector Decision: SFTP vs API for SOC2 Artifacts

Team —

Legal has reviewed the high-level options and is comfortable with the S3 presigned URL pattern if we mandate encryption-at-rest, scoped cross-account roles, and a documented retention/transfer SLA in the MOU. For customers who cannot provision cloud storage (air-gapped or on-prem), Legal supports a one-off SFTP agreement with tighter logging and a shorter retention window.

Proposal for a pilot:
1) Test bucket: Redwood to create a dedicated test S3 inbound (us-west-2) with server-side encryption (KMS-redwood-soc2) and lifecycle rules.
2) ClearPath to demonstrate pull flow + log correlation using request-id.
3) Run a 2-week transfer of sample artifacts (max 250MB each).
4) Validate audit events and retention behavior, then sign MOU addendum.

I've attached a short pilot checklist we can use. (Attachment: pilot-checklist.md (MD))

—Grace
Head of Compliance Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Schultz <matthew.schultz@clearpathgrc.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final Decision & Next Steps: Hybrid S3+API Pilot

Matthew —

Thanks for the options and the quick turnaround. Redwood's decision: run a hybrid pilot that uses an inbound S3 ingestion pattern as the primary delivery mechanism and an API pull/callback flow for low-latency artifacts. SFTP will remain an opt-in fallback for on-prem/air-gapped customers under a scoped agreement.

Immediate next steps:
- Redwood to provision a test inbound bucket in us-west-2 (server-side encryption with KMS-redwood-soc2) and share cross-account role ARN with ClearPath by 2026-03-29.
- ClearPath to provide proof-of-concept: one successful pull + request-id in response headers by 2026-04-02.
- Both teams to run the 2-week sample transfer and surface any retention/logging gaps.

Please confirm timeline and I'll loop in legal/engineering owners to get the MOU addendum drafted.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running.

—Olga
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: sftp-credentials-template.csv referenced as fallback template)
